code.originalText: Eight-week review: blood count, methylmalonic acid, iron studies, the endoscopy biopsies and surveillance

text.paragraph: Eight-week review: blood count, methylmalonic acid, iron studies and the biopsy results. [S]

Admiral Peary returns eight weeks after starting treatment. He feels close to his old self, walks a mile with his stick and has no breathlessness. The tingling has mostly gone, but the ends of his feet remain numb and he is still unsteady in the dark. He has given himself all his weekly injections. He has had no falls and no new foot wounds. The biopsies from his endoscopy show autoimmune atrophic gastritis: atrophy of the body of the stomach with intestinal metaplasia and enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia, a normal antrum, no Helicobacter pylori on special stains, and no neuroendocrine tumor or dysplasia. He has no indigestion and no black stools. [S]

list.item:
Pernicious anemia on weekly cyanocobalamin (D51.0). Full hematologic response at eight weeks: hemoglobin 14.1 g/dL and MCV 91 fL, with methylmalonic acid and homocysteine back to normal. Vitamin B12 itself does not need rechecking. [S]
Continue weekly injections while the nerves are still improving.

Autoimmune atrophic gastritis (K29.40). Confirmed by biopsy, with intestinal metaplasia in the body of the stomach and no neuroendocrine tumor or dysplasia. Autoimmune gastritis carries a higher risk of type 1 gastric neuroendocrine tumors and, to a lesser degree, of gastric adenocarcinoma. The best surveillance interval is uncertain; with extensive atrophy and metaplasia, he and Dr. Lindgren-Okafor chose endoscopy every three years. [S]
Repeat upper endoscopy in three years, sooner for indigestion, vomiting, black stools, weight loss or new anemia.
TSH every year, since autoimmune thyroid disease often accompanies autoimmune gastritis.

Iron deficiency (E61.1). Ferritin has fallen from 62 to 24 ng/mL and transferrin saturation to 14% as new red cells use the iron stores, and an acid-poor stomach absorbs iron poorly. The colonoscopy and endoscopy showed no bleeding source. [S]
Ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day with orange juice, apart from tea and coffee.
Ferritin and transferrin saturation at the fifteen-week review; intravenous iron if oral iron fails.

Subacute combined degeneration (G32.0). Steady recovery of vibration and balance; numbness at the ends of the feet persists. [S]
Continue physical therapy.
